name: App Tamer
product: App Tamer by St. Clair Software

evidence.says: The release notes date App Tamer 2.8.4 to August 6, 2024 and list it as the download.
St. Clair Software calls 2.8.4 the latest release and explicitly says that 2.6 and later are universal builds running natively on Intel and Apple Silicon.

notes: The vendor reports universal support starting with 2.6, earlier than both versions in the scanner history.

name: OverSight_Installer
product: OverSight installer by Objective-See

evidence.says: Objective-See labels OverSight_Installer.app as the installer for the OverSight tool and lists 1.2.0 as a legacy release.

notes: The scanned bundle is the setup and upgrade utility for OverSight.

name: Eclipse-inst
product: Eclipse Installer (Oomph) by the Eclipse Foundation

evidence.says: The Eclipse Foundation lists separate macOS x86_64 and AArch64 downloads for the JRE-bundled Eclipse Installer 2026-09 R and describes its interactive package selection.
Eclipse's product metadata identifies the installer in the 2026-09 R distribution as 1.42.0.
Eclipse's 2026-09 R file index dates the Apple Silicon installer image to September 1, 2026.
The Eclipse Foundation dates the general availability of the 2026-09 release to September 1, 2026.

notes: This is the JRE-bundled Oomph Eclipse Installer, distributed as 2026-09 R, with an interactive UI for choosing and managing Eclipse packages.

name: SAP GUI for Java Installer
product: SAP GUI for Java Installer (SAP SE)

evidence.says: The archived scan’s Info.plist identifies SAP SE’s com.sap.platin.installer 1.0.0 bundle and names its executable install.
SAP identifies PlatinGUI platform packages as distributing or installing SAP GUI for Java and describes the Mac disk image with the ready-to-copy client.

notes: The scanned executable belongs to the installer bundle; the installed SAP GUI for Java client is a separate listing candidate.

name: Pinegrow
product: Pinegrow Web Editor (Pinegrow)

evidence.says: Pinegrow’s October 13 release notes for version 10.1 link separate Apple Silicon and Intel macOS builds.

name: InVision Studio
product: InVision Studio (InVision)

evidence.says: The UK Competition and Markets Authority cites InVision’s Studio sunset notice and documents that InVision withdrew the screen design software in 2023.

limitation: The final Mac release and its binary architecture were not confirmed.
notes: The old InVision site redirects to Miro.

name: TiddlyDesktop
product: TiddlyDesktop by the TiddlyWiki project (Jeremy Ruston and contributors)

evidence.says: The project publishes TiddlyDesktop release v0.0.22.
The latest official release is v0.0.22 and publishes distinct Mac Apple Silicon and Mac Intel ZIPs.
Homebrew disabled its v0.0.22 cask because it failed the Gatekeeper check.

notes: The upstream Apple Silicon ZIP remains listed, while Homebrew disables its cask because of Gatekeeper.

name: DazCentral
product: DazCentral content manager by Daz 3D

evidence.says: Daz 3D identifies DazCentral as its own separate content manager.
The Daz forum reproduces Daz staff's announcement that the company was phasing out DazCentral in favor of Daz Install Manager.
The Daz forum documents the 2023 discontinuation and a user finding that the download path led to Daz Install Manager.

limitation: The final DazCentral version and its architecture were not verified.
notes: Daz Install Manager replaced DazCentral for content and software downloads.

name: eso
product: The Elder Scrolls Online Mac game client by ZeniMax Online Studios

evidence.says: ZeniMax's associate director of community confirms that the Mac game client runs as an Intel app via Rosetta on Apple Silicon.
The ESO game director's October 2026 announcement confirms reliance on Intel binaries and targets summer 2027 for the native Apple Silicon client.
ZeniMax labels the November 9, 2026 live release Update 51 Incremental 2.

limitation: ZeniMax published the update label, and the bundle's numeric build number remains unverified.
notes: Vendor-confirmed Rosetta operation applies to the shipped Mac game client. Official ARM support is planned for summer 2027.

name: ZeniMax Online Studios Launcher
product: The Elder Scrolls Online launcher by ZeniMax Online Studios, using Solid State Networks software

evidence.says: A Mac crash report identifies com.solidstatenetworks.host as the ZeniMax Online Studios Launcher inside the ESO installation.

notes: This bundle is the game's launcher and patcher. The separate eso listing covers the playable game client.

name: cd to
product: cd to… by Jay Tuley

evidence.says: Jay Tuley's v3.1.3 release notes call it a universal binary for Apple Silicon and Intel.
GitHub's release metadata dates the developer's v3.1.3 release to April 5, 2022.

notes: The Finder toolbar app opens Terminal in the current directory.

name: SoundID Reference
product: SoundID Reference standalone systemwide application by Sonarworks

evidence.says: Sonarworks states that native Apple Silicon support shipped on May 24, 2022 and applies to all public versions from 5.3.0 onward.
Sonarworks dates 5.13.9.1362 to November 12, 2026 and lists macOS fixes under the main SoundID Reference app.

name: Gobbler2
product: Gobbler desktop client by Gobbler Media Inc.

evidence.says: Marketplace partner Solid State Logic confirms that Gobbler Media ceased trading and shut down its subscription platform on November 1, 2023.
Marketplace partner Slate Digital confirms the platform's closure and the end of Gobbler support for its subscriptions on November 1, 2023.

limitation: The final Mac version and its architecture were not verified.
notes: The desktop client was tied to the Gobbler audio plug-in subscription marketplace.

name: Mail for Gmail
product: Mail+ for Gmail (formerly Mail for Gmail) by Rocky Sand Studio Ltd.

evidence.says: Apple's Mac App Store lists Rocky Sand Studio's Mail+ for Gmail 2.1 dated September 25, 2025 and shows the scanned 1.1.1 in the same release history.
MacUpdater records both Intel and Apple Silicon architectures for build 40 of version 2.1 under the exact scanned bundle ID.

limitation: Architecture is documented by MacUpdater's app inventory.
notes: The release history lists an interim EasyMail name before the current Mail+ for Gmail branding.

name: Superpowered
product: Superpowered calendar and AI meeting notetaker by Superpowered Labs

evidence.says: The developer’s download page states that Superpowered is no longer available for download.
The developer identifies the product as its Mac and Windows AI meeting notetaker and calendar tool.
Superpowered's co-founder advertised an earlier Mac release supporting Intel and Apple Silicon without stating its binary architecture.

limitation: The final version and final build architecture could not be established.
notes: The co-founder listed both Mac processor families at the AI Notes launch. The final Mac build architecture is unknown.

name: findMyStock
product: 选股好帮手 Free (findMyStock Lite) by Yuchens

evidence.says: Apple’s catalog matches the exact bundle ID to the Mac stock-screening app and lists version 1.40 dated February 11, 2017.
The App Store page still lists the Mac stock-screening app.

limitation: No architecture statement or inspectable official package surfaced for the exact Mac App Store build.

name: 3CX client
product: 3CXPhone / legacy 3CX Client for Mac (3CX)

evidence.says: 3CX’s regional support manager confirms the Mac desktop app was discontinued in V20 and says the legacy clients cannot be provisioned on V20.
The archived submissions identify the legacy 3cxphone14 Mac bundle and record x86 for the scanned 16.0.1 and 15.1.1 builds.

limitation: The final release and architecture of the 3cxphone14 bundle are unconfirmed.
notes: 3CX directs current Mac users to its web client or PWA.

name: Fleetsmith
product: Fleetsmith Mac agent UI (Fleetsmith, later Apple)

evidence.says: Apple states that on October 21, 2022 it ended Fleetsmith and its devices stopped receiving configuration profiles from the Fleetsmith server.

limitation: The final Mac agent build and its architecture were not verified.
notes: The scanned bundle was the management agent’s UI.

name: PSequel
product: PSequel PostgreSQL client (PSequel Project)

evidence.says: The developer’s linked PSequel.1.5.3.app.zip was inspected and its PSequel.app/Contents/MacOS/PSequel main executable is x86_64 only.
Multiple users report crashes on database connection on Apple Silicon, including a translated x86_64 1.5.3 crash in the bundled ODBC library.

limitation: The app can launch under Rosetta, and some users report success after manually replacing the bundled ODBC library.
notes: The disposition covers the official unmodified build and its core database connection function.

name: DAZStudio
product: Daz Studio 4.x Pro by Daz 3D

evidence.says: Daz Software identifies 4.24.0.4 as the general release of Daz Studio 4.24 and dates it to December 29, 2025.
Daz's Mac FAQ discussion describes Studio 4.x as dependent on Rosetta 2 on Apple Silicon.
A user posted a Daz Studio 4.24.0.4 startup log from a Mac mini with an Apple M4 Pro chip.

limitation: The matching 4.24.0.4 user log is from the Public Build channel, and the stable executable was not inspected.
notes: Daz Studio 6 is a separate beta release line.

name: SizeUp
product: SizeUp by Irradiated Software

evidence.says: Inspection of SizeUp.app/Contents/MacOS/SizeUp found x86_64 and i386 slices in the exact 1.7.4 bundle.
Homebrew documents that version 1.7.4 is Intel-only and requires Rosetta 2 on Apple Silicon.
The vendor’s HTML release history dates version 1.7.4 to September 22, 2018.

name: WifiMouseServer
product: WifiMouseServer by Vivid Designs

evidence.says: Vivid Designs links its WifiMouse Android desktop companion's Mac disk image.
The developer's release metadata identifies WifiMouseServer.dmg as the Mac asset under release tag 1.
Static inspection of WifiMouseServer.app in the official disk image matched bundle ID com.yourcompany.WifiMouseServer and found only x86_64 in Contents/MacOS/WifiMouseServer.

limitation: The bundle plist has no version number, and Rosetta operation was not verified.
notes: The inspected asset is the Mac download linked by the vendor from the GitHub release tagged 1.

name: RadarScope
product: RadarScope 4 for Mac (Base Velocity, DTN)

evidence.says: Apple’s store lookup for the former standalone RadarScope Mac listing returned zero results.
DTN documents the move from RadarScope 4 for Mac to RadarScope 5 and distinguishes their subscription handling.
Apple identifies the current RadarScope 5 App Store listing as com.basevelocity.RadarScope.
The archived standalone Mac scan identifies com.basevelocity.mac.RadarScope 4.2.2 and reports an x86 binary.

limitation: The final RadarScope 4 build number and its architecture were not confirmed.
notes: The vendor directs Mac users to RadarScope 5, which uses a different bundle ID and store listing.

name: iDefrag
product: iDefrag (Coriolis Systems)

evidence.says: Coriolis says it shut down in 2019, lists 5.3.1 for macOS 10.12–10.13 as its newest museum build, and says the archived products have no support.
The archived official iDefrag-5.3.1.dmg was inspected and its iDefrag.app/Contents/MacOS/iDefrag executable is x86_64 only.

notes: The last build is Intel-only and remains available from the vendor’s museum.

name: Stonesoft VPN Client
product: Forcepoint NGFW VPN Client for macOS (formerly Stonesoft VPN Client)

evidence.says: Forcepoint's older notes identify the scanned 2.0.1 build 1013 as the Stonesoft VPN Client for its NGFW.
Forcepoint's release index lists 2.7.0 as its current macOS VPN Client release.
Forcepoint specifies version 2.7.0 build 20260325 and provides a SHA-512 digest for its official macOS package.
The downloaded package matched Forcepoint's SHA-512, and static inspection found the scanned bundle ID and both arm64 and x86_64 in Contents/MacOS/Forcepoint NGFW VPN Client.

notes: The rebranded app retains com.stonesoft.VPNClient. Build 20260325 is documented, but a separate release date was not found.

name: Mixbus32C-7
product: Mixbus32C version 7 by Harrison Consoles

evidence.says: Harrison lists 7.2.0, dated November 3, 2021, as its final archived Mixbus32C 7 release.
A February 2022 user report describes running the non-native Mixbus32C on an M1 Pro MacBook Pro.
Harrison's 8.1 announcement introduces native ARM builds as new and explicitly identifies the Intel build as the Rosetta option.
Harrison's current Mixbus release has a dedicated ARM download.

limitation: The M1 report predates the native release and omits the exact 7.x build number.
notes: The record covers the version-specific 7.x bundle. Harrison separately distributes native builds of the later Mixbus line.

name: WD Discovery
product: WD Discovery desktop drive manager (Western Digital)

evidence.says: The SanDisk forum notice dates the end of WD Discovery support and downloads to July 31, 2025.
Western Digital documents WD Discovery as its drive-management tray application.

limitation: The final macOS release and its architecture were not confirmed.

name: 1player
product: 1player by Kongfu Apps

evidence.says: The scanned bundle identifies 1player and its exact Kongfu Apps bundle ID.
Apple’s Mac software catalog lookup returns no U.S. result for the exact bundle ID.

limitation: No live vendor release, current binary architecture or official discontinuation notice could be found.

name: Tdx TdxiMac
product: 国泰君安证券锐智版 (Ruizhi for Mac), Tongdaxin build for Guotai Junan Securities

evidence.says: Tongdaxin lists Guotai Junan’s dedicated Ruizhi Mac edition among its brokerage-specific distributions.
The historical listing identifies the exact Mac product and points to its former official disk image.

limitation: The historical vendor download host no longer resolves, and no current version or architecture was verifiable for this exact brokerage edition.
notes: The current broker download page highlights its separate 富易 Mac product.

name: Ludo-desktop
product: Ludo-desktop by CronlyGames Inc.

evidence.says: The original scan identifies the exact standalone Ludo-desktop bundle as com.cronlygames.ludo.mac.
Apple’s U.S. Mac catalog lookup returns no result for the scanned bundle ID.
Apple identifies the available CronlyGames Mac Ludo Online edition as version 2.2.7 with bundle ID com.cronlygames.usludo.mac.

limitation: The current availability, continuity and architecture of the exact scanned bundle could not be verified.

name: DHF3.0
product: 大黄蜂云课堂 Mac player / DHF3.0 (Shenzhen Chaoshidai Software)

evidence.says: The vendor labels its standalone Mac player Intel-only and offers an Apple-chip link to the separate App Store edition.
Inspection of the vendor-linked DHF_Player_Mac_5.3.4.zip found a com.chaoshidai.macDHF bundle reporting 5.4.7 and an x86_64-only 大黄蜂云课堂.app/Contents/MacOS/大黄蜂云课堂 main executable.
Apple’s lookup identifies the App Store player under the separate bundle ID com.chaoshidai.player.

limitation: No reliable Rosetta report was found for the desktop bundle, and the website’s March 18, 2026 date is attached to the differently labeled 5.3.4 download.
notes: The website and ZIP filename say 5.3.4, while the enclosed app’s Info.plist says 5.4.7 (build 20260313).

name: Yuque App
product: Yuque desktop knowledge base / 语雀 (Ant Group)

evidence.says: The vendor page’s download data links public Mac installer 4.2.1.1333 and lists no architecture for it.
The Yuque cask uses the same numbered DMG and names com.yuque.app preference files without specifying an architecture or Rosetta requirement.
MacUpdater records both Intel and Apple Silicon slices for the exact Yuque bundle ID in the older 4.1.7 release.

limitation: The current public Mac DMG is approximately 197 MB and was not eligible for binary inspection under the brief’s limit.
notes: The unrelated aDrive and Alipay Key Tool cask hints do not identify Yuque. MacUpdater confirms Apple Silicon architecture for the older 4.1.7 build.

name: Snip
product: Snip screenshot utility by Tencent Technology (Shenzhen)

evidence.says: Tencent’s own download page lists Snip 2.0 as the latest version.
Inspection of Snip.app/Contents/MacOS/Snip inside Tencent’s 2.0 installer found an x86_64-only executable and its Info.plist matched com.tencent.snip.
Tencent’s Mac App Store history dates version 2.0 to November 30, 2012.

limitation: Rosetta launch and screenshot capture were unverified.

name: XPS-to-PDF Lite
product: XPS-to-PDF Lite by RootRise Technologies Pvt. Ltd.

evidence.says: The historical listing links the free Lite edition to its own Mac App Store product ID 849734925.
Apple’s catalog returns no current result for the Lite edition’s original store ID.
The developer’s current portfolio lists XPS to PDF while omitting the separately distributed Lite edition.

limitation: The final version and final build architecture were unverified.
notes: The separately listed XPS-to-PDF edition uses bundle ID com.RootRiseTechnologies.XPS-to-PDF.

name: iPastels
product: iPastels by Norbyte

evidence.says: Norbyte’s Mac App Store listing advertises native Apple Silicon for current version 5.6.3 and explicitly names native M1 support in the version 5.1 notes.
Norbyte’s own iPastels site points Mac users to that App Store listing.

notes: The current cross-platform App Store release uses com.norbyte.iPastels, and its version history includes 4.7 and the subsequent Universal Purchase change.

name: WiFiMasterKey
product: WiFi万能钥匙 Pro (WiFiMasterKey) by Lantern / LinkSure Network

evidence.says: The vendor promotes its current desktop app under the name WiFi连网助手.
Apple identifies that currently listed Mac app as version 1.8.0 with bundle ID com.wifi.security.
Apple’s Chinese Mac software catalog lookup returns no result for the original com.lantern.wifimasterkey bundle ID.

limitation: No current official release or architecture evidence was found for WiFi万能钥匙 Pro itself.
notes: The current WiFi连网助手 distribution has Apple Silicon and Intel downloads for its own desktop product.

name: Toggl Track
product: Toggl Desktop 7 / Toggl Track legacy Mac client (Toggl)

evidence.says: Toggl’s archived repository states that rewritten Mac and Windows clients superseded this project and that feature development on it ended.
The original client’s official Mac stable download points to TogglDesktop-7_5_441.dmg.
The legacy Mac changelog dates stable version 7.5.441 to January 20, 2021.
The tagged project specifies x86_64 for the release target with ID com.toggl.toggldesktop.TogglDesktop.
The later 7.5.490 Mac prerelease target still specifies x86_64 for that bundle ID.

notes: Version 7.5.441 is the final stable download listed for this bundle, with later archived prereleases including 7.5.490. The rewritten Toggl clients are separate from this listing.

name: Lantern
product: Lantern legacy Mac client (GetLantern / Brave New Software Project)

evidence.says: The archived scan identifies the original Mac bundle as com.getlantern.lantern with a lowercase lantern executable and supplies no version.
Lantern support distinguishes the new version 9 app from users’ legacy pre-9 app and provides an account transition path.
The publisher archived its older downloads here and directs users to its main Lantern repository for releases starting at version 9.
Inspection of this official DMG found Lantern.app/Contents/MacOS/Lantern to be universal x86_64 and arm64 in 8.3.7, with the different bundle ID org.getlantern.lantern.
The current version 11.0.0 Mac build configuration also names the org.getlantern.lantern bundle.

limitation: The last release and architecture under com.getlantern.lantern remain unconfirmed.
notes: Treat the current Lantern app as a separate bundle. Homebrew’s old Rosetta caveat disagrees with the inspected 8.3.7 main executable.

name: Internxt Drive
product: Internxt Drive for macOS by Internxt

evidence.says: Internxt publishes release 2.7.1.90 for macOS.
Inspection of Internxt Drive.app/Contents/MacOS/Internxt Drive in the official image verified arm64 and x86_64 Mach-O headers with macOS 13.5 minimum targets.
Internxt’s release history documents the macOS client’s version 2.0 rewrite in SwiftUI and File Provider integration.

notes: The rewritten Mac client uses internxt.InternxtDesktop. Its CFBundleShortVersionString is 2.7.1 and the vendor release tag is 2.7.1.90.

name: Aunbox ScreenRec
product: 嗨格式录屏大师 (HiFormat Screen Recorder) by Auntec / Aunbox

evidence.says: Auntec’s download center offers the Mac desktop recorder, with channel 39094a17 served to macOS visitors.
The vendor’s current Mac download channel identifies package 2.8.9.308.
Inspection of the official Mac disk image verified arm64 and x86_64 in ScreenRec.app/Contents/MacOS/ScreenRec, with bundle com.aunbox.ScreenRec and app version 2.8.9.

notes: The verified 2.8.9 app comes in package 2.8.9.308. Some vendor articles cite 3.68.0.1, while the public Mac download channel served the inspected 2.8.9 bundle.
